Page 1/7 
Machine Learning (BMI/GEO/WNA) 
Code Assignment U1A1  
Linear Regression 
This is NOT a group Assignment. 
 
10 marks 
Please complete seeing the videos for Week 1-2 before attempting this 
assignment.  
 
Use real estate valuation regression dataset : 
https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/477/real+estate+valuation+data+set  from 
the UCI repository, and use google colab to code. 
 
First, download the csv file, and open it in your computer and analyze the data. 
Try to understand what the data is about. Read through the data description 
given 
in 
the 
UCI 
website 
as 
well. 
 
Section A 
Answer the following questions [1 mark if you answer all the below questions] : 
1. How many samples are there? 
There are 414 samples 
2. How 
many 
input 
variables 
are 
there? 
There are 6 input variables 
3. Which 
column 
is 
the 
output 
variable 
(target 
outcome)? 
Y house price of unit area is output variable 
4. What 
does 
each 
of 
the 
input 
columns 
mean 
? 
Input columns are the independent variables on which the 
output/target variable depends. The target variable varies with respect 
to 
each 
input 
variable.

Page 2/7 
Section B 
For each of the questions below, you need to put in the screenshot of the code 
and its output. You could use the sample google colab file that is provided with 
this assignment. 
 
1. Understanding the dataset [4 marks] 
There are many input variables in this dataset. Use only X1 to X4 as input 
variables, and y as the output variable. 
Using the scatter plots between each of the input features (X1-X4) and the 
output (Y), which input variable, do you think, is better in predicting the output 
/ target variable ? 
 
Input feature 1

Page 4/7 
 
Input feature 4 
 
 
The input feature 3 (distance to the nearest MRT station) is better in predicting 
the output variable. The plot obtained is positively skewed. It shows a trend

Page 5/7 
where the target variable that is house price decreases with increase in input 
feature 3. 
 
2. Write code to find out how many samples are there in total in this dataset? [1 
mark] 
 
 
 
3. What is the train test split ratio that you have chosen ? [1 Mark] 
 
 
Train test split ratio - 8:2 
 
4. Evaluate the linear regression model by computing the MAE, MSE and Mean 
Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) . 
(for MAPE - pls refer to the sample here - https://scikit-
learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.metrics.mean_absolute_percent
age_error.html)

Page 6/7 
[3 marks] 
MAE, MSE, MAPE of linear regression model for input variable 3 (distance to 
the nearest MRT station) 
 
 
5. What are the 3 new things that you learned after you completed this 
assignment ? 
 
• Providing more sample for training does not ensure better output 
variable prediction 
• The MSE, MAE, MAPE varies according to the train test ratio that one 
provides 
• Low MSE value does not mean most predicted output will match the 
actual traget variable value in the test set

Time - 4 hours max.
